messages:
maria: Heads-up: after rolling adaptive-kernel-routing for mixed-quant (INT4 + FP8) to canary, our token-quality eval delta jumped on the structured-output suite. Not catastrophic but consistent across 3 runs.
naresh: which canary? config name?
maria: canary name = adaptive-routing-v2, commit c3f9d2b. routing heuristics now pick low-latency kernels for short context, fallback to fp8-kernel for longer seqs.
sophia: any signs of KV-cache mismatch? last time we saw structured JSON breakage it was stale KV padding.
maria: good point. initial repro uses seq_len=1024, streaming enabled, KV caching on. Failures: truncated JSON fields and occasional hallucinated keys. Eval delta ~+6% hallucination rate on the JSON-API eval set.
jordan: bench-bot ran the canary perf sweep this morning, attaching summary?
bench-bot: perf-run/1913578000: adaptive-routing-v2 vs baseline-v1. Throughput: +12% for p50 short-ctx, p95 latency +2ms. Model CPU/GPU utilization shifted: more kernel switches per request (avg 1.9 -> 3.6).
naresh: more kernel switches could explain KV cache invalidation frequency. If we switch kernel mid-request, are we preserving cache layout and dtype?
maria: that's the suspicious part. runtime logs show a few warnings: `kv_cache_realloc: dtype_mismatch detected, promoting to fp32 buffer` — happened ~0.4% of requests in canary.
sophia: that matches hallucination spikes. Promotion can nuke quantization state for subsequent tokens. Any repro logs with model trace?
maria: attaching minimal repro snippet here:
```
# repro driver (pseudo)
client = RedwoodClient(canary='adaptive-routing-v2', streaming=True)
resp = client.generate(prompt, max_tokens=256, seq_len=1024)
print(resp.text)
```
jordan: can we bisect to the kernel-selection change specifically? c3f9d2b touches both heuristics and kernel registry ordering.
naresh: I'll instrument the path that switches kernels to emit `kernel_handoff={from,to}, kv_dtype={dtype_before,dtype_after}, cache_version` for a few requests. Low overhead.
maria: thanks. Also we should run the eval suite with KV cache disabled to isolate. If hallucinations go away, it's cache interaction.
sophia: agree. I'll run a quick sweep: (1) baseline-v1 with cache on, (2) adaptive-v2 with cache on, (3) adaptive-v2 with cache off.
bench-bot: eval-suite/1913578200: run queued. ETA ~18m.
deploy-bot: Canary adaptive-routing-v2 still 12% of traffic in region us-west-2. You can pause via `/canary pause adaptive-routing-v2`
maria: pausing now until we have root cause. /canary pause adaptive-routing-v2 :warning:
naresh: instrumenting now. If it's dtype promotion, likely a kernel selection that doesn't honor quantized buffer layout. Might be an ABI mismatch between int4 kernels and fp8 kernels in the KV layer.
jordan: note for triage: prioritize correctness > perf. If we need a quick mitigation: avoid handoff for long-seq streaming requests (force single kernel path) or disable promotion path.
sophia: preliminary eval results: adaptive-v2 w/ cache on shows +5.8% hallucinations; adaptive-v2 w/ cache off drops to +0.6% (within noise). Baseline-v1 w/ cache on is nominal.
maria: that's pretty conclusive for cache+handoff interaction.
naresh: found two suspicious spots in kernel_registry: `select_kernel()` returns kernel_meta but the caller wasn't setting `kv_dtype` when crossing quantization families. Adding small patch to propagate dtype through handoff.
maria: can you run a smoke with that patch on a developer build?
naresh: yes, running smoke now on staging with a reproducer.
bench-bot: smoke/1913578600: 50 runs: no `kv_cache_realloc` warnings, avg latency similar.
jaordan: if smoke looks good, do a small canary restart with the patch, but keep traffic low.
maria: plan: 1) naresh pushes patch -> dev smoke 2) sophia runs full eval-suite with canary off 3) if good, restart canary at 2% and monitor eval/job metrics 4) keep rollback plan ready.
sophia: noted. I'll run the full eval after naresh confirms smoke.
naresh: patch pushed to branch `fix/kv-dtype-propagation` (PR#4123). Running extended smoke now.
maria: thanks. Also add a short unit test that simulates kernel handoff with mixed dtype buffers so this doesn't regress.
naresh: on it.
bench-bot: extended-smoke/1913579120: 500 runs, 0 warnings, no regressions in the structured-output suite.
maria: re-enabling canary at 2% after deploy checklist. /canary resume adaptive-routing-v2 2%
deploy-bot: adaptive-routing-v2 resumed at 2% in us-west-2. Monitoring dashboards active.
jordan: leave the canary running for at least 2 hours with continuous eval gating. If anything drifts revert to baseline.
maria: thanks team. Postmortem if anything else pops. For now tagging this thread: triage/quant-kv-handoff.
naresh: saving logs and traces under /mnt/triage/1913578420/traces.txt
sophia: will follow up with the eval diffs and the unit test PR link.
maria: closing for now, will re-open if new signals appear. :white_check_mark:
